label: Combinatorics
shortDescription: The art of counting, arranging, and optimizing discrete structures.
modulesDescription: Read the combinatorics chapters in order, or jump directly to the topic you need.
ogDescription: Master combinatorics: basic counting, permutations and combinations, binomial coefficients, pigeonhole and inclusion-exclusion, generating functions, Catalan/Stirling/Bell numbers, graph coloring, Ramsey theory, extremal graphs, enumerative techniques, Young tableaux, matroids, flows, linear programming, probabilistic method, Lovász Local Lemma, and additive combinatorics — with ELI5 explanations, worked examples, and practice questions.
courseDescription: A complete combinatorics course covering the fundamental principles of counting (product/sum rules, permutations, combinations), advanced counting with generating functions and recurrence relations, special numbers (Catalan, Stirling, Bell), graph-theoretic combinatorics (coloring, Ramsey, Turán, Szemerédi), enumerative methods (bijective proofs, Young tableaux, hook-length), combinatorial optimization (matroids, matchings, network flows, linear programming), and advanced probabilistic and algebraic tools (probabilistic method, Lovász Local Lemma, combinatorial nullstellensatz, additive bases). Features intuitive ELI5 sections, detailed step-by-step worked examples, common mistakes, and targeted practice questions for each lesson.

topics.title: Counting Principles
topics.description: The rules every count rests on: bijections, the sum and product rules, pigeonhole, inclusion–exclusion and double counting.

topics.title: Basic Counting
topics.description: Permutations, combinations and the binomial coefficients, with the identities that follow and the models they each apply to.

topics.title: Generating Functions
topics.description: Formal power series as a bookkeeping device for counting, and the recurrences they solve in closed form.

topics.title: Special Sequences
topics.description: Fibonacci, Catalan, Stirling, Bell, Eulerian and the partition numbers — what each counts and how each is computed.

topics.title: Partitions, Young Tableaux and RSK
topics.description: Integer partitions drawn as diagrams, the hook-length formula that counts their standard fillings, and the RSK correspondence.

topics.title: Graph Coloring and Ramsey Theory
topics.description: Colouring vertices and edges, the chromatic number and its bounds, and the Ramsey results that make disorder impossible.

topics.title: Extremal Graph Theory
topics.description: How many edges a graph can carry before a forbidden subgraph is forced: Turán's theorem, its corollaries and what follows.

topics.title: The Probabilistic Method
topics.description: Proving a structure exists by showing a random one works, sharpened by deletion and by the Lovász Local Lemma.

topics.title: Algebraic and Additive Combinatorics
topics.description: Polynomials as a counting tool — the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz — and the structure of sumsets from Cauchy–Davenport onward.

topics.title: Matroids and Matchings
topics.description: The structure that makes the greedy algorithm correct, and the matching theory of Hall and König that mirrors it.

topics.title: Flows and Linear Programming Duality
topics.description: Max-flow min-cut, the algorithms that realise it, and the linear programming duality that explains every min–max theorem here.
